cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host, revocation ON, guest default preserved: the sequence COMPLETES. NOT CAUGHT. pool-0-36 reported `FF2 status=0 events=1 metadata=1472 payload=128`, runner exit 0, 7 of 7 cases passed. The mechanism, now evidenced rather than argued: a buffer returned to an AVBufferPool never reaches free(), so it never enters the quarantine the revoker sweeps and the sweep has nothing to find. THE CONTROL FIRED IN THE SAME BOOT, which is the bar the retraction set and the one the withdrawn claim never met: revocation-control reported `REVOCATION_CONTROL revocation=1 tag_after_sweep=0 reissued=1` and then FAULTED -- SIGPROT, si_code 2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG), addr=pc=0x101dc0, equal to the address supervise resolved for mc_defect_read independently of the run. So the revoker demonstrably sweeps in this guest, and a completion here is 'the mechanism is active and did not fire' rather than 'the mechanism is absent'. The platform controls passed alongside it: cheribsd-abi `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1`, cheribsd-bounds CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY. THIS IS THE READING THAT 18a16640682b CLAIMED AND NEVER TOOK -- see the `retraction` field below, which is kept rather than deleted. The predicted OUTCOME was right; what was wrong was asserting it had been observed. It has now been observed. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, stated here because the retraction below says the cited runner 'cannot produce it' and a reader should not take that as 'unmeasurable': the reading was taken by running the SAME purecap pool-security binary through ports/common/host/cheribsd/run.py with --runtime-revocation on. What cannot produce it is the port's own PoisonCap wrapper, whose unconditional literal 'off' at poisoncap/run.py:129-130 is the specific thing the retraction withdrew a citation to.

cheribsd-revocation.retraction:
RETRACTION, 2026-10-06. This arm previously asserted a MEASURED completion on stock CheriBSD with libc revocation ENABLED, introduced by 18a16640682b ("Measure the stock-CheriBSD arm instead of deriving it", on origin/dev) and carried forward by 3f3abf676e58. Three specific claims are withdrawn:
  (1) that the reading was measured at all;
  (2) the citation `case: pool-0-36/37/38`. Those names are constructed at exactly one place, ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/host/cheribsd/poisoncap/run.py:70, and that runner's only call site passes the unconditional literal `"--runtime-revocation", "off"` at :129-130 -- unchanged at every revision of the file's existence. So the cited names belong to a mode-0 PoisonCap run whose revocation policy is the OPPOSITE of this arm's stated target.
  (3) the control reading `runtime_revocation=1`, and `guest_default: preserved`. ports/common/host/cheribsd/run.py:119-120 builds the abi probe's expectation FROM the policy, so under `off` the required marker is `runtime_revocation=0`; and :195-199 launches every case under `env _RUNTIME_REVOCATION_DISABLE=1`, which overrides a preserved kernel default in the test process (ports/common/host/cheribsd/README.md:151-159; bug-corpora/cpython/pymalloc-repros/runners/cheribsd/README.md:102-107). The committed bundle that does hold pool-case records, ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/results/measurements/20260919-poisoncap-pilot/pool-isolated-1.json, reads `runtime_revocation: off` and `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=0`, and its case list stops at pool-2-13 -- cases 36-38 entered the runner in 6891936e52f3, AFTER that pilot.
SCOPE, stated precisely: no artifact of this reading exists anywhere in the tree (searched by identifier across all refs; the only two files containing `pool-0-36` are a case.json and this corpus's README), and the runner these case names come from cannot produce it. What cannot be proven from the tree is that no uncommitted ad hoc run ever happened -- a direct invocation of ports/common/host/cheribsd/run.py with a hand-rolled cases.json would need no code change. So the claim withdrawn is "this was measured and here is the run", not "no such run is conceivable".

native-detect.requires: the port's payload arena is one allocation, so ASan's silence here would measure the fixture rather than FFmpeg
native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O0; port library built with the same flags). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 67108864` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 67108864` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (3ef5169ae90b); the arm was previously 'not written'.

backing.role: the informative negative: revocation exists here, at the backing allocation, and the pool never frees its backing but recycles out of it. This separates 'no mechanism' from 'a mechanism at the wrong point'
